Installed packages: JSON3, CairoMakie, Makie and Julia standard libraries (including Base64, Statistics, LinearAlgebra, Random). messages.user:
Write a program that reads from standard input. The first line contains the name of the column to analyze. The remaining lines form a CSV representation of a table (including header and rows). The program must assess whether the distribution of values in the specified column is uniform and visualize this distribution using a histogram.

Specifically:
- If the table is empty, the specified column does not exist, or the column contains only null values, the program prints:
    The DataFrame is empty or the specified column has no data.
  and generates a blank histogram titled:
    Distribution of values in [column_name] (No Data)
- Otherwise, the program determines if the count of each unique value in the column is identical:
    • If yes, it prints: The distribution of values is uniform.
    • If no, it prints: The distribution of values is not uniform.
  In both cases, it generates a histogram showing the frequency of each value, with one bin per unique value, black edges, alpha=0.7, labeled axes ("Values", "Frequency") and title:
    Distribution of values in [column_name]

Output (stdout) is only the message. The histogram is created but not displayed or saved.

Input format example:
Category
Category
A
A
B
B
C
C

Expected output:
The distribution of values is uniform.
